meaning: A work works if what it draws and labels is true to the 874 rows: each bridge stands where it really is and when it was really built, its colour matches its own rating, and its labels name the right things, so a reader is not misled about any column.

items.why: The left-hand map spreads the bridges over a rectangle rather than the shape of Delaware, so 'each bridge where it stands' is not true.
The 'where' panel is stretched into a rectangle and the county labels are in the wrong places (Sussex sits at the northern end).
The map keeps Delaware's shape, the Delaware River crossing is labelled correctly, and the stacks by year carry plausible ratings (new bridges good, old ones mixed).
The map, the counties, the legend counts (41/335/374/114/7/3) and the Delaware River callout (3,291 m, 1951) all agree with each other and with the data.
The layout is the same as W03, but the ratings are attached to the wrong bridges: the newest bridges come out 'fair', the 1910s–40s bridges 'very good', and the Delaware River bridge changes colour.
The 'where' panel stretches the state into a rectangle, so the bridges are not drawn where they stand.
The 3,291 m 1951 Delaware River bridge is labelled 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem', a road name that does not belong to that crossing.
The map is stretched sideways out of Delaware's shape, and its callout points at the wrong place.
The caption says the oldest bridge, built 1839, crosses the SR 1 Milford bypass, a road far newer than the bridge, so the fields are mismatched; the map is also a rectangle.
The 'rated poor' dots sit on bridges coloured good and are placed differently from the other versions, so the dots and the ratings contradict each other.
The map keeps Delaware's shape, the arcs' colours agree with when the poor bridges were built, and the legend totals add to 874.
It matches W03: the geography, the labels and the per-bridge ratings all hold together.
The colours are shuffled: compared with the correct versions, the poor-rated arcs have moved to recent bridges and the map has lost its fair and poor colours.
The left-hand map is a rectangle of scattered bridges rather than Delaware, so the positions are false.
The map has Delaware's shape, the counties sit in order north to south, and each poor dot falls on a red-rated arc at the same latitude in both panels.
It matches W15: correct geography, county labels, and consistent ratings and dots.
The map is a rectangle, the three county labels are piled on top of each other, and the long-bridge callout names a ramp instead of the Delaware River.
The map is distorted, the county labels overprint each other, the 3,291 m bridge is mislabelled 'Mispillion River, 1939', and the stack colours are reshuffled.
The map is out of shape, the county labels collide in one spot, and the Delaware River callout's leader line runs to a bridge in the middle of the state.
The map is stretched far too wide for Delaware, so the bridges are not drawn where they stand, even though the year stacks are right.
